stories.title: USDA-backed sawmill breaks ground in Clatskanie
stories.summary: Construction has officially begun on a new sawmill in Clatskanie, backed by $30 million in USDA-guaranteed financing for Clatskanie Scion LLC to expand Sheridan-based Myers Woodline. The mill is expected to create at least 35 jobs and start up in about 18 months — a rare new mill in a state that lost seven mills in 2024 alone.
stories.img_credit: Photo: Columbia County Spotlight (the story's own photo, via Oregon Civic Newsstand).

stories.summary: The Tribune's running roundup of confirmed holiday dates is out: the Christmas Ships pass St. Helens on Dec 12 and Scappoose Bay on Dec 13, the Scappoose Spirit of Christmas Parade is Dec 5, and Michael Allen Harrison plays Columbia City on Nov 30. The Keep It Local Wonderland Bazaar lands Nov 28 with more than 40 local vendors and free Santa photos.

stories.title: Vernonia posts the county's biggest test-score jump — English proficiency up 13 points in one year
stories.summary: Vernonia School District posted the largest one-year gain of any district in the county on state tests: 45.1% of students met the English language arts standard last spring, up from 32.0% a year earlier. The jump earned Vernonia a state literacy-tour “model school” recognition, and the district shared the results with the community at an engagement night on Nov 18.

stories.title: County auctions 31 odd lots — a burned-out mobile home, mineral rights and a landlocked parcel — with opening bids from $368
stories.summary: The county put 31 county-owned properties up for auction in the St. Helens justice facility lobby on Nov 17, from a burned-out double-wide on a floodplain lot in Vernonia to nine mineral-rights-only parcels in the hills west of Vernonia. Minimum bids were set at what the county is owed rather than market value — about $189,000 in minimums against $1.74 million in assessed value — and the county first published the wrong minimum bids and had to correct them.

stories.title: Columbia River Treasures reopens in Rainier after a three-week closure
stories.summary: The Rainier vintage shop is back open after an unexpected three-week closure while the owners handled medical issues. The shop at 113 E 1st St is freshly stocked for the holidays, with vintage Christmas decor, stockings and Santa mugs alongside Pendleton mugs, cozy flannels, Carhartt hoodies, jeans and graphic tees. Open Saturdays and Sundays, 12 to 6 PM.
